Paolo expressed a concern that kvm_mmu_zap_mmio_sptes() could have a
quadratic runtime[1]
column2: i.e. restarting the spte walk while zapping only

column1: MMIO sptes could result in re-walking large portions of the list over
and over due to the non-MMIO sptes encountered before the restart not
being removed.
At the time
column2: the concern was legitimate as the walk was restarted when

column1: any spte was zapped.  But that is no longer the case as the walk is now
restarted iff one or more children have been zapped
because zapping children makes the active_mmu_pages list unstable.
Furthermore
column2: it should be impossible for an MMIO spte to have children

column1: i.e. zapping an MMIO spte should never result in zapping children.  In
other words
column2: kvm_mmu_zap_mmio_sptes() should never restart its walk

column1: so should always execute in linear time.  WARN if this assertion fails.
Although it should never be needed
column2: leave the restart logic in place.

column1: In normal operation
column2: the cost is at worst an extra CMP+Jcc

column1: some reason the list does become unstable
crash KVM
